allow_large: The owner asked on 2026-09-28 for Luna max as the default subagent of every Codex worker kind; it touches forge.toml, init's template, the models check and their tests
done_when: This repo's forge.toml and the forge.toml that forge init writes give [models.lite] subagents gpt-6-luna with subagent_effort max, like build and fix, and a test through forge work shows a fix's first Codex round passing them

findings.body: The generated forge.toml now always includes these Codex subagent keys. If a client later changes `workers` to `claude` and selects a Claude lite model, `forge work` still refuses the first fix: `src/forge/worker.py:178-182` rejects any Claude worker whose model entry has `subagents`. This is a compatibility edge case; the requested Codex behavior works.
findings.title: Switching an initialized repo to Claude blocks its first fix

findings.body: This new test runs `forge init` and checks the lite keys already asserted by the changed `tests/test_codex_reader.py:164-173`, which checks the entire generated models table. Removing this duplicate leaves that contract covered and keeps the separate `forge work` test as the behavior proof.
findings.title: Simpler: remove the duplicate forge init test → keep the existing init assertion

why: A fix's first Codex round runs as the lite kind, which sets no subagents, so it gets no Luna max helpers while story tasks and fix rounds do
